lal_pensioner.text: I laid bricks on the Rock from 1962. In June 1969 they closed the gate and I had no job the next morning. Neither did thousands of us.
Some went to work in Germany, some to the shipyards. I went to Algeciras, then back to the Rock in 'eighty-five, older and slower. The walls I built are still standing. I check.

lal_moroccan.text: When the Spanish workers could no longer cross, Gibraltar brought in workers from Morocco. I came over in 1970 and stayed fifty years.
So I'm part of the story too. A frontier closes in one place and a ferry opens in another. I come here on Fridays for the cards, and because the coffee's better. Don't tell Gibraltar.

lal_teacher_es.text: ¡Hola! I teach English to the workers and Spanish to the visitors, so everyone in this room owes me money.
Start with 'hola', hello, and 'buenas', the lazy Andalusian good day. 'Por favor' is please, 'gracias' is thanks, and 'perdón' gets you through any queue.
Andalusians often drop the 's' at the end of a word: 'gracias' can come out like 'gracia'. Don't correct them. You're the one with the accent here.
